sources.citation: Fodor, István. 1975. Pallas und andere afrikanische Vokabularien vor dem 19. Jahrhundert: Ein Beitrag zur Forschungsgeschichte. Hamburg: Buske. Section 7.91 'Mangree', pp. 162-164 (full transcription hosted at Wikipedia:WikiProject Languages/Mangree source).
sources.note: Nothing. Fodor reprints Oldendorp's 11 words, notes 'OLD gibt keinen Beispielsatz aus dem Mangree an', discusses possible Twi/Ewe/Kru/pidgin look-alikes, and concludes 'So bleibt das Mangree unidentifiziert.' No phonological commentary beyond the name's pronunciation (mangre: / mangrɛi). (Transcription saved as the.wiki file; the printed book itself was not opened.)

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Mangree language' (raw wikitext, accessed 2026-09-17); cites Fodor 1975 and Latham 1848 (BAAS 17th report p.176, repeats 3-4 words incl. 'ichi' water).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; states the language 'is only attested in a list of a dozen words collected in the late 18th century' and cannot be classified.

sources.citation: Oldendorp, Christian Georg Andreas. 1777. C.G.A. Oldendorps Geschichte der Mission der evangelischen Brüder auf den caraibischen Inseln S. Thomas, S. Croix und S. Jan, Theil 1. Barby: Laux. (BSB scan on archive.org, id 11129612bsb; scanned text)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The primary source: an ethnographic note on the 'Mangree' nation (pp. 276-277: neighbours of the Kanga, a large river separates them from the Gian, languages 'wenig verschieden') and 11 concept words in the comparative vocabulary table (Gott Jankombum, Himmel Tata, Sonne Lataa..). No sentences, no numerals, no remarks on pronunciation or accent.

sources.citation: Oldendorp, C.G.A. 2000 [1767-1777]. Historie der caribischen Inseln Sanct Thomas, Sanct Crux und Sanct Jan: kommentierte Ausgabe des vollständigen Manuskriptes (ed. G. Meier, S. Palmié, P. Stein, H. Ulbricht), 4 vols. Berlin: VWB (Abhandlungen und Berichte des Staatlichen Museums für Völkerkunde Dresden 51).
